entities.name: Foodborne Trematodes
entities.description: A group of zoonotic helminthiases caused by digenetic flukes (liver flukes: Clonorchis sinensis, Opisthorchis viverrini/felineus, Fasciola hepatica/gigantica; lung flukes: Paragonimus westermani; and intestinal flukes) acquired through consumption of raw or undercooked freshwater fish, crustaceans, or aquatic plants, leading to chronic hepatobiliary, pulmonary, or ectopic diseases.

entities.name: Ingestion of Raw or Undercooked Freshwater Cyprinid Fish
entities.description: Dietary consumption of raw, undercooked, pickled, fermented, or sun-dried freshwater cyprinid fish (such as carp dishes, Thai koi pla, or Chinese raw fish porridge) harboring encysted metacercariae of Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis species.

entities.name: Ingestion of Raw or Undercooked Freshwater Crustaceans
entities.description: Dietary consumption of raw, undercooked, salted, marinated, or wine-soaked freshwater river crabs or crayfish (such as drunken crabs) containing encysted metacercariae of Paragonimus westermani or related lung fluke species.

entities.name: Ingestion of Raw Freshwater Aquatic Plants
entities.description: Ingestion of raw, unwashed wild aquatic vegetables (particularly watercress [Nasturtium officinale], water spinach, water chestnuts, or mint) or untreated surface water contaminated with encysted metacercariae of Fasciola hepatica or Fasciola gigantica in livestock-grazing regions.

entities.name: Freshwater Snail Intermediate Host Aquatic Environment
entities.description: Ecological exposure to freshwater aquatic habitats harboring specific snail species that serve as mandatory first intermediate hosts required for trematode larval multiplication and cercarial shedding.

entities.name: Consumption of Raw Paratenic Wild Boar Meat
entities.description: Ingestion of raw or undercooked meat from paratenic mammalian hosts (such as wild boars) that feed on freshwater crustaceans, transmitting viable Paragonimus metacercariae.

entities.name: Clonorchis sinensis
entities.description: The Chinese liver fluke, a digenetic trematode dwelling within intrahepatic bile ducts for up to 20-30 years, causing chronic mechanical ductal injury, adenomatous hyperplasia, recurrent pyogenic cholangiohepatitis, and cholangiocarcinoma.

entities.name: Opisthorchis viverrini
entities.description: The Southeast Asian liver fluke, highly endemic in the lower Mekong basin, dwelling within intrahepatic bile ducts and designated as an IARC Group 1 biological carcinogen causing cholangiocarcinoma.

entities.name: Opisthorchis felineus
entities.description: A liver fluke endemic to Russia and Eastern Europe that parasitizes intrahepatic bile ducts and the gallbladder following consumption of raw cyprinid fish.

entities.name: Fasciola hepatica
entities.description: The common sheep liver fluke, a large trematode (20-30 mm) that penetrates Glisson's capsule and burrows through hepatic parenchyma during an acute invasive phase before colonizing the major biliary tract in its chronic phase.

entities.name: Fasciola gigantica
entities.description: The giant liver fluke, a zoonotic parasite endemic in tropical regions of Africa and Asia causing acute destructive hepatic parenchymal tunneling and chronic biliary obstruction.

entities.name: Paragonimus westermani
entities.description: The Oriental lung fluke, whose juvenile flukes penetrate the peritoneal cavity and diaphragm to encapsulate in pairs within pulmonary parenchyma connecting with bronchioles, or migrate aberrantly to the central nervous system.

entities.name: Recurrent Biliary Colic with Marked Eosinophilia
entities.description: Cardinal clinical presentation of hepatobiliary fluke infection characterized by right upper quadrant abdominal pain, intermittent obstructive biliary colic, and marked peripheral blood eosinophilia.

entities.name: Rusty-Brown Sputum with Operculated Fluke Eggs
entities.description: Pathognomonic expectoration of thick, gelatinous 'chocolate-sauce' or rusty-brown sputum containing clotted blood, Charcot-Leyden crystals, and masses of operculated Paragonimus eggs.

entities.name: Acute Invasive Hepatic Tunneling Syndrome
entities.description: Acute presentation of fascioliasis occurring 1-12 weeks post-ingestion, characterized by high continuous or spiking fever (39-40°C), painful hepatomegaly, severe right upper quadrant tenderness, urticaria, facial angioedema, and massive leukocytosis.

entities.name: Intrahepatic Cholangiocarcinoma in Chronic Fluke Carriage
entities.description: Definitive malignant transformation of intrahepatic and perihilar biliary duct epithelium into cholangiocarcinoma driven by chronic Clonorchis sinensis or Opisthorchis viverrini irritation, parasite granulin secretome, and endogenous nitrosamines.

entities.name: Ectopic Cerebral Paragonimiasis with Adult-Onset Focal Seizures
entities.description: Severe neurological complication of Paragonimus migration through craniocervical connective tissue, presenting with adult-onset focal epilepsy, visual field defects, intracerebral hemorrhage, and chronic intracranial hypertension.

entities.name: Massive Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia (>40-80%)
entities.description: Striking admission hematologic hallmark, reaching 40-80% of total differential count (absolute eosinophil count 10,000-35,000/μL) with marked leukocytosis in acute invasive fascioliasis, and 15-35% in paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Markedly Elevated Serum IgE Concentration
entities.description: Admission serologic hallmark routinely exceeding 1,000 to 5,000 IU/mL, reflecting intense Th2-mediated helminthic immune activation during active fluke tissue migration.

entities.name: Disproportionately Elevated Serum ALP and GGT with Mild Transaminitis
entities.description: Admission liver chemistry pattern demonstrating marked elevations of Alkaline Phosphatase (ALP) and Gamma-Glutamyl Transferase (GGT) with mild-to-moderate transaminitis (AST/ALT 2-4x ULN) and direct hyperbilirubinemia during biliary obstruction.

entities.name: Branching Serpentine Hypoechoic Hepatic Tracks on Ultrasound
entities.description: Bedside abdominal ultrasound hallmark revealing linear, branching, serpentine hypoechoic parenchymal tunnels and burrows in the subcapsular liver parenchyma during acute juvenile Fasciola migration.

entities.name: Diffuse Uniform Peripheral Intrahepatic Bile Duct Dilation on Ultrasound
entities.description: Bedside ultrasound hallmark of chronic clonorchiasis demonstrating diffuse, non-tapering dilation of peripheral intrahepatic bile ducts with enhanced periductal echogenicity while the common bile duct remains of normal caliber.

entities.name: Ring-Shaped Cystic Pulmonary Lesions on Admission Chest Radiography
entities.description: Triage chest X-ray findings in pulmonary paragonimiasis showing 1-3 cm round, ring-shaped cystic lesions with thin or thick walls, patchy nodular opacities, pleural thickening, or spontaneous pneumothorax.

entities.name: Multilocular Soap-Bubble Calcifications on Brain CT/MRI
entities.description: Pathognomonic neuroimaging finding in cerebral paragonimiasis demonstrating clustered, multilocular, calcified cystic lesions with ring enhancement forming a distinctive 'soap-bubble' appearance.

entities.name: Sputum Microscopy Demonstrating Operculated Paragonimus Eggs
entities.description: Triage microscopic examination of unstained sputum wet mount demonstrating large (80-120 x 45-65 μm), golden-brown, thick-shelled operculated eggs with an opercular collar rim.

entities.name: Stool Concentration Microscopy Demonstrating Urn-Shaped Fluke Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic stool examination by Kato-Katz or formalin-ether concentration revealing small (25-35 x 12-19 μm), yellowish-brown, pitcher/urn-shaped operculated eggs with an expanded shoulder collar and abopercular knob, diagnostic of Clonorchis or Opisthorchis.

entities.name: Stool Microscopy Demonstrating Large Operculated Fasciola Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic identification of large (130-150 x 65-90 μm), golden-yellow, unembryonated operculated eggs in stool or duodenal aspirates during the chronic biliary phase of fascioliasis.

entities.name: Complete Absence of Dietary Freshwater Seafood or Aquatic Plant Exposure
entities.description: Total absence of dietary history involving raw or undercooked freshwater fish, crustaceans, wild aquatic vegetables (watercress), or unboiled pasture surface water, which virtually excludes foodborne trematode infection.

entities.name: Total Absence of Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia (<3%)
entities.description: Normal peripheral blood eosinophil count (<3% or normal absolute count) in an acutely symptomatic patient with fever, right upper quadrant pain, or pulmonary infiltrates, which strongly excludes acute fascioliasis and acute paragonimiasis.

entities.name: Acid-Fast Bacilli Detection on Sputum Smear or GeneXpert without Eosinophilia
entities.description: Microbiological confirmation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis by acid-fast smear or GeneXpert PCR in the absence of peripheral eosinophilia, effectively excluding pulmonary paragonimiasis in a cavitary lung presentation.

entities.name: Solitary Round Hepatic Liquefactive Cavity with Positive Amoebic Serology
entities.description: Demonstration of a single round liquefactive liver abscess containing anchovy-paste pus with positive Entamoeba histolytica serology and zero eosinophilia, excluding acute fascioliasis.

entities.name: Acoustic-Shadowing Choledocholithiasis with Neutrophilic Leukocytosis
entities.description: Sonographic demonstration of acoustic-shadowing gallstones in the common bile duct accompanied by marked neutrophilic leukocytosis without eosinophilia, ruling out biliary fluke disease in favor of calculous cholangitis.

entities.name: Pulmonary Tuberculosis
entities.description: A mycobacterial pulmonary infection that mimics pulmonary paragonimiasis with chronic cough, hemoptysis, and cavitary infiltrates, but lacks peripheral blood eosinophilia, lacks operculated sputum eggs, and tests positive for acid-fast bacilli.

entities.name: Amoebic Liver Abscess
entities.description: A protozoan hepatic infection caused by Entamoeba histolytica presenting with high fever and tender hepatomegaly, differentiated from acute fascioliasis by a solitary round liquefactive abscess, positive amoebic serology, lack of branching parenchymal tracks, and absence of eosinophilia.

entities.name: Acute Bacterial Cholangitis with Choledocholithiasis
entities.description: Bacterial biliary infection secondary to choledocholithiasis presenting with Charcot's triad (fever, jaundice, RUQ pain), differentiated from liver fluke disease by acoustic shadowing stones on ultrasound, neutrophilic shift without eosinophilia, and absence of raw fish dietary history.

entities.name: Praziquantel Therapeutic Susceptibility in Clonorchiasis, Opisthorchiasis, and Paragonimiasis
entities.description: Rapid clinical and parasitological response to oral praziquantel (25 mg/kg TID for 2-3 days), achieving >85-100% cure rates in Clonorchis sinensis, Opisthorchis viverrini, and Paragonimus westermani by inducing tegumental disruption and spastic paralysis.

entities.name: Triclabendazole First-Line Cure in Fascioliasis
entities.description: Oral triclabendazole (10 mg/kg single dose or 20 mg/kg divided dose taken with food), which exhibits unique fasciolicidal efficacy against both juvenile migratory and adult Fasciola flukes, producing rapid defervescence and >95% cure.

entities.name: Intrinsic Praziquantel Refractoriness in Fascioliasis
entities.description: Total lack of therapeutic response (0% cure rate) of Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica to standard or high-dose praziquantel regimens due to their exceptionally thick tegumental architecture, resulting in persistent infection and clinical treatment failure.

entities.name: Refractoriness to Standard Broad-Spectrum Antibacterials
entities.description: Total failure of broad-spectrum beta-lactam antibiotics, cephalosporins, or antimalarials to achieve clinical defervescence or resolve symptoms in patients with acute or chronic foodborne trematode infections.
